column3: “With whatever verdict” becomes “in the way”; “with whatever measure you measure” becomes “by your standard of measure.”
Close to the Greek; “speck” and “log” as in v. 3.
NASB renders “bread” as “a loaf” and turns the question expecting “no” into a plain question.
NASB keeps the question expecting “no” with a closing “will he?”
NASB recasts the verse: “treat people the same way you want them to treat you.”
NASB follows the reading “for” (Textus Receptus) rather than the critical text’s “how” (“how small the gate”); “compressed” is rendered “narrow.”
NASB recasts the question in the passive (“Grapes are not gathered …, are they?”) and renders “thorns” as “thorn bushes.”
NASB adds “will enter” at the end to complete the sentence.
Close to the Greek; “depart from Me …” is in capitals as an Old Testament quotation.
NASB follows the critical text with “may be compared” (“will be likened”); “does them” is rendered “acts upon them.”
NASB renders “beat upon” as “slammed against” and adds “and yet.”
Close to the Greek; NASB has “their scribes,” as in the critical text.
